The plan's pinned Lean Challenge Statement for stepOk/stepOk_sound types the world argument as World (Fin 4) (LS (Fin 4) Nat) (Msg Nat). That signature is UNIMPLEMENTABLE: Distsys.Exec.Net N M = Packet N M -> Prop has no Decidable instance, so deliver's w.net.mem p premise cannot be decided from a World. The same plan's Decision 4 and report 02 Finding 3 say the opposite -- 'an executable SimWorld mirror with an abstraction into World, NOT decide over World'. The two are in direct conflict; Decision 4 was followed and stepOk takes the mirror, with the pinned CONCLUSION recovered unchanged at ew.toWorld. Nothing is weakened, but the pinned block's argument type is departed from and needs a user ruling.

Distsys.Bracha.applyLabel, which the plan's pinned stepOk_sound names as the successor-world function, is the IDENTITY on .env (.drop _), .env (.duplicate _) and .env (.corrupt _ _) -- its own book needed only the inject case. The plan's run 2 (crash below the bound) drops a crashed node's in-flight packets, so a checker stated over that applier could never accept it. Resolution: a checker-local total applier Distsys.Replay.applyLbl that agrees with Bracha.applyLabel wherever that one is not identity-on-env (proved as applyLbl_eq_applyLabel) and additionally pins the three further byzAllowed cases that ARE deterministic. tamper, the only nondeterministic action, stays outside the alphabet.
